mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the Federal Funds rate above 5% in the month prior to the decision point reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during similar high-inflation regimes (t-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which raises consumer confidence and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% in a month while UNRATE falls by >0.2 percentage points
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant correlation with the labor strength signal (Pearson IC > 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average in the prior quarter indicates accelerating economic demand, which anticipates a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 12-month MA for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative despite INDPRO exceeding its MA (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) over three months suggests deflationary pressure, lowering real discount rates and generating negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls by >2% over three consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during prior deflationary episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 1-month change in the GDP deflator (not in the catalog, so use GDPC1 as proxy for inflation) turns positive while the Federal Funds rate remains steady, it indicates a shift toward price stability, prompting a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly change > 0 and FEDFUNDS unchanged for the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are flat or negative despite the inflation signal (IC < -0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in the monthly average hours worked per capita (HOUST) combined with a rise in job openings (not in catalog - so use PAYEMS as proxy for labor market tightness) suggests labor market stress, which can lead to equity market volatility and negative 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls by >2% in a month while PAYEMS increases by >5%
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly more negative than during prior tightness episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 305) the S&P 500 20-day forward return tends to be negative, regardless of other macro signals, due to discount rate premia.
failure_condition: In high-inflation regimes the 20-day forward return is not statistically lower than the average of low-inflation regimes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline in both industrial production (INDPRO) and consumer confidence proxies (none available - so use a combination of RSAFS and UNRATE as a proxy for weak demand) over two months predicts negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns as market anticipates contraction.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for two consecutive months and RSAFS < 700,000 while UNRATE > 4%
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly more negative than during prior contractionary demand episodes (IC > -0.15).
